back: A depreciation improves the trade balance if |PEDx| + |PEDm| > 1.
The trade balance worsens at first after a depreciation and improves later as quantities adjust.

front: Effect of a depreciation on AD?
back: Net exports rise, so AD shifts right.

front: Effect of a depreciation on SRAS?
back: Imported inputs are dearer, so SRAS shifts left.

front: Effect of a depreciation on the price level?
back: It tends to rise: imported inflation and extra demand.

front: Effect of an appreciation on exporters?
back: Exports become dearer abroad, so sales and competitiveness fall.

front: Why can a depreciation fail to improve the trade balance?
back: Low elasticities (Marshall-Lerner not met), time lags, imported inflation and retaliation.

front: Change in quantity from a price change?
Why is exchange rate policy not a substitute for supply-side policy?
back: Any competitive gain is eroded by inflation unless productivity improves.
